alerts.title: Uncontrolled hypothyroidism despite levothyroxine
alerts.message: Patient has TSH 12.4 mIU/L (target below 4.5) with low Free T4, indicating inadequate hypothyroidism treatment. She reports often forgetting the thyroid tablet, which is the likely primary cause. Symptoms include tiredness, feeling cold, constipation, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, and delayed ankle reflexes—all consistent with hypothyroidism. The clinician's plan to continue levothyroxine 50 mcg without addressing adherence or dose adjustment is insufficient. Uncontrolled hypothyroidism can also contribute to weight gain, hyperlipidemia, and low mood, compounding the DTG weight gain concern.

evidence.recommended_action: Counsel on levothyroxine adherence and escalate dose (e.g., 75–100 mcg). Recheck TSH in 6–8 weeks. Hypothyroidism may be contributing to weight gain and dyslipidemia.

alerts.title: DTG weight gain attribution confounded by hypothyroidism
alerts.message: Guidelines note DTG is associated with weight gain and hyperglycemia risk, especially in patients with BMI ≥25. Patient gained 12 kg over 3 years on TLD with BMI now 33. However, uncontrolled hypothyroidism (TSH 12.4, low Free T4) is a significant alternative or contributing cause of weight gain, fatigue, and constipation. The plan to switch from DTG for weight gain should first address hypothyroidism, as weight gain may stabilize once thyroid function is corrected. Premature DTG switching risks losing the benefits of viral suppression and high genetic barrier.

evidence.recommended_action: Optimize hypothyroidism treatment first before attributing weight gain solely to DTG. Reassess weight after thyroid stabilization before deciding on ART switch.

alerts.title: Dyslipidemia and hyperglycemia screening under DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines require hyperglycemia screening for DTG patients with ≥2 risk factors (age ≥30, BMI ≥25). Patient has both risk factors plus BMI 33. Fasting glucose 5.6 mmol/L is borderline. LDL 4.2, total cholesterol 6.4, and triglycerides 2.3 mmol/L are all elevated. Uncontrolled hypothyroidism is a known cause of secondary dyslipidemia and may also affect glucose metabolism, compounding DTG metabolic risks. The clinician's plan does not address monitoring or managing these metabolic abnormalities.

evidence.recommended_action: Monitor fasting glucose every 3 months for 6 months. Address dyslipidemia after thyroid optimization. Consider cardiovascular risk assessment and lifestyle counseling.

alerts.title: Overdue TDF renal monitoring
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring every 12 months for patients on TDF. The last creatinine was 196 days ago (2025-08-12), so annual monitoring is not yet overdue but is approaching. The clinician's plan does not include renal monitoring today despite the patient being on TDF for 3 years. TDF can cause chronic kidney disease, Fanconi syndrome, and decreased bone mineral density. Current creatinine of 72 umol/L appears acceptable, but no eGFR was documented.

evidence.recommended_action: Ensure serum creatinine and eGFR are checked at or before the 12-month mark from the last test (due by August 2026). Document eGFR with creatinine results.
